After that I took a hiatus from writing, eventually finding my way back in 2011 when a Halloween short story bled into a new novel.

I'm happy to say I've hit 2/10 for my adult fiction and 2/10 for my kid's books. It's funny, because today I actually finished the first draft of my second kid's book. I hope to have it published by mid-October and do a giveaway for Halloween.

So, here's what I came up with trying to answer that question while driving for an hour (shower thoughts don't have to occur in the shower).

I'm sure there's an answer or it's a stupid question, but either way, I refuse to look up that answer until I share what idea I had.

Basically, a sphere is a circle in 3D. If you take two circles, and lay one along the X & Y axes (so it would appear flat, pressed against the X axis plane), and the other along the X & Z axes (so it would appear flat, pressed against the Y axis plane), and overlay them such that one bisects the other at a 90 degree angle (where their center is the origin), the degrees of those two circles can represent any direction. You don't need a circle along the Y & Z axes because the combination of the other two can represent a degree in that direction.

So, figuring out how many degrees a sphere has is as simple as 3602. That sounds right to me, but I'm sure it's retarded in some way. For example, at the point where both circles intersect, they'd share the same degree. So you'd have to subtract 1 for each point where they intersect along their edges (they do it twice, so it's now 3602-2), so you wouldn't count the same degree twice.

So my answer is that a sphere has 129,598 degrees. That doesn't sound right, but I don't know enough about math to debate it.
